about: Register of every committed data file in magpie/cwplans: where its data came from, under which licence, and how it uses OpenStreetMap (ODbL). Checked by tools/check-data-register.mjs, which also writes DATA-REGISTER.md. Add an entry before committing a new data file.

policy.personal_org_address_data: Restrictions suspended for this project during scoping, planning and prototyping (owner, October 2026; CLAUDE.md, Data ethics, exception).
policy.licence_limit: Never fetch or commit proprietary, restricted-licence or virally licensed data.
policy.crawls: Website crawls, direct and via the Internet Archive or Common Crawl, are fair use for scoping (owner, 2026-10-03). Each crawl-derived file names its method and date here. Re-check before anything leaves the prototyping phase.
policy.knowledge_graph: Owner, 2026-10-03: selected sources will later go through a data integration pipeline into a knowledge graph. So every source keeps a stable key here (with licence, URL and fetch date), every transform is an activity in pipeline.json (what it used, what it generated, its rules), and identifiers are kept as they come from the source (OSM ids, Wikidata QIDs, UPRNs, TOIDs, FHRS ids, company numbers, cwb- ids) so they can become IRIs. tools/check-data-register.mjs --write exports pipeline.jsonld (PROV-O, DCAT, Dublin Core).
policy.odbl: OpenStreetMap data (ODbL 1.0, share-alike) is allowed for now (owner, 2026-10-03). Its use is to be reviewed in full during planning and prototyping. Every committed file that holds OSM data, or data derived from it, is listed here with osm.use other than 'none'.

Re-check before anything leaves the prototyping phase.

crawl.method: direct HTTP GET with User-Agent "glitchcan-cwplans/0.1 (https://github.com/danbri/glitchcan-minigam)", robots.txt obeyed (RFC 9309), one request at a time per host at least 1.5 s apart, at most 4 hosts at once; canarywharf.com pages read only as Internet Archive id_ copies (fetched by fetch-cwg.mjs on 2026-10-03 and reused)

web-structured-data.name: schema.org structured data (JSON-LD, microdata, RDFa) published on the web pages of the entities the registry tracks: occupant, brand, store and charity sites

web-structured-data.note: Crawl for scoping, allowed by the owner (2026-10-03: "Website crawls - direct and via IA or CommonCrawl etc are fair use for our scoping purposes."). Store-finder searches with UK postcodes allowed by the owner (2026-10-03: "we are permitted per industry convention to submit storefinder forms with UK postcodes"). Only the structured-data blocks, page title, final URL, status and a hash of the rendered HTML are kept; no full pages are committed. Re-check before anything leaves the prototyping phase.

crawl.method: headless Chromium (Playwright) with a desktop Chrome User-Agent plus " glitchcan-cwplans/0.1 (+https://github.com/danbri/glitchcan-minigam)"; robots.txt obeyed (RFC 9309) for every page navigation and redirect; at most 3 pages at once, one page at a time per host, at least 2 s between page loads on a host; images, media and fonts not loaded; load + network idle (20 s cap) + 1.5 s; cookie banners accepted only when a page showed no structured data; store finders searched once per brand and branch postcode; Internet Archive copies of canarywharf.com pages read from the local fetch-cwg.mjs cache with scripts off (no request)
